elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how the Hindi language reflects traditions and social distinctions to do with how people are regarded in society, how old they are or what religion they practise, for example, the use of the honorific particle जी after a family name to show respect

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how particular gestures, terms and expressions have embedded cultural meanings and can convey feelings, beliefs and values, for example, the use of the expression फिर मिलेंगे when leaving, in order to avoid the finality associated with ‘goodbye’

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that there is a standard form of Hindi called मानक हिंदी used for writing, and spoken by many people, as well as a variety of spoken dialects that differ from region to region, for example, ब्रज, अवधी, राजस्थानी

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how culture and identity are expressed in Hindi-speaking communities, and comparing this with other cultures, for example, noticing the different regional words used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples to identify themselves, such as Zenadth Kes, Koori, Koorie, Noongar and Nunga, and comparing this with Hindi-speaking cultural groups

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying similarities and differences in Indian folk and tribal dance and music with other cultures, for example, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander dance and music

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that different regions in India and other countries where Hindi is spoken may have different cultural practices and beliefs, for example, decorating the main entrance of the house and celebrating the harvest festival

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing familiar Indian language and cultural practices maintained over a long time, for example, traditional hospitality, अतिथि देवो भवः, or the singing of the national anthem

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and discussing the importance of music and dance in Indian culture(s) as an expression of identity and emotions, such as national pride, happiness, love, joy and sadness, for example, folk dance, folk music, Hindi films and classical music

elaborations.name: VC2LH4U04-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the meaning of culture and identity, for example, using a diagram to show the visible elements such as ways of celebrating, dress, traditions, symbols, manners, routines and behaviours, and the less-visible elements such as preferences and values

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 5 and 6, Hindi language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students continue to communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers in purposeful, creative and structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They interact in Hindi to exchange information and ideas within their interests, school and local environment, and engage with Hindi-speaking communities in person or in secure, teacher-moderated online environments. Background language learners and second or additional language learners may also work independently and/or in groups to collaborate and share learning, with support. Students continue to receive ongoing support from modelling and from digital and print resources.

Students engage with a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts that may include stories, posters, images, notes, invitations, video clips and procedural texts. Background language learners may share authentic resources from their local community with their peers.

Students recognise how the Devanāgarī script affects pronunciation and meaning. They identify language structures and features of Hindi, and use familiar metalanguage to reflect on their understanding. They recognise that some words and expressions are not easily translated, and reflect on how diverse cultural practices, behaviours and values influence communication and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 6, students initiate and use strategies to maintain interactions in Hindi that are related to their personal worlds and school environment. They use appropriate sound combinations, intonation and rhythm in spoken texts. They collaborate in spoken and written activities to share and discuss information, preferences and ideas. They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in Hindi or English, adjusting their response to suit purpose.

Students use modelled structures when creating and responding in Hindi. They create texts, selecting and using a variety of vocabulary and sentence structures and the Devanāgarī script to suit different contexts, and using conventions appropriate to text type. They apply rules for pronunciation and intonation in spoken language and apply conventions of spelling and punctuation in written language. They compare language structures and features in Hindi and English, using familiar metalanguage. They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6C01 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to their personal worlds and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating conversations, commencing with a greeting, enquiry about wellbeing, current or past activities, or news, for example, तुम/आप कैसे हो/हैं?; आपने पिछले सप्ताह/सप्ताहांत मे क्या किया?; घर मे सब कैसे हैं?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing conversation skills such as staying on topic, requesting more information, recognising non-verbal cues or using interjections, for example, क्या यह सच है?; दिलचस्प है …; मुझे बताओ; अच्छा!; आप इस विषय में क्या सोचते हैं?; मुझे ऐसा लगता है …; क्या हम इस बात पर चर्चा कर सकते हैं?; आहा! यह अच्छी बात है; तो ठीक है …; अच्छा; ओहो!; अरे वाह!

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing personal experiences, preferences and opinions, and expressing agreement or disagreement in a respectful manner, for example, रमा, मुझे माफ़ करना लेकिन मुझे लगता है कि …; सच पूछो तो मेरे विचार में; मैं इस बात से सहमत हूँ कि …

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some colloquial expressions and idioms to enhance interactions when describing people, places or experiences or to express feelings, for example, अँगुली पर नचाना; नाक में दम करना; मेरी चाची मुझसे बहुत प्यार करती हैं; मैं उनकी आँखों का तारा हूँ; अपने घर में कुत्ता भी शेर होता है

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing with peers the experience of communicating in Hindi in the classroom context compared with at home or in the community, for example, मुझे हिंदी पढ़ना अच्छा लगता है लेकिन सबके सामने बोलने में झिझक होती है

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting information using a range of interrogatives and open-ended questions to elicit further details and clarify points (e.g. कैसे, क्या, कब, कहाँ), and exchanging written communication such as emails, secure, teacher-moderated chat or messages, for example, तुम शनिवार को क्या कर रहे हो?; इस काम में …; मुझे लगता हैं कि हमें यह लिखना चाहिए

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in secure online exchanges such as video calls with sister schools in India, to describe and compare routines, interests and activities, and to share experiences of learning Hindi in Australia, for example, आप सुबह कितने बजे उठते हैं?; आपकी पाठशाला कितने बजे शुरू होती है?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for, giving and following instructions or directions, and giving feedback in a variety of situations, varying language to suit formal or informal contexts, for example, शिक्षिका ने कहा है कि शांत बैठो; यहाँ आकर सबके साथ बैठो

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C01-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: requesting assistance or clarification from peers and teachers, checking on each other’s progress and indicating understanding, for example, नहीं, मुझे समझ नहीं आया। कृपया फिर से दोहराइए।; यह बहुत कठिन है। इस में मुझे क्या करना है?; जी हाँ, मैं समझ गई। यह तो बहुत आसान है।; ठीक है। सब ख़त्म हो गया? अभी नहीं, पर जल्द ही हो जाएगा।; आप समझते हैं, है न?; आप कितनी तेज़ी से लिख सकते हैं?

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6C02 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion and planning with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phrases to seek permission, ask questions, or borrow items from peers or the teacher, for example, क्या मैं शौचालय जा सकता हूँ?; क्या मैं तुम्हारी पेंसिल ले सकता हूँ?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in authentic or simulated exchanges and transactions that involve Indian currency, such as ordering in restaurants or buying items from street vendors, using appropriate gestures, expressions and negotiation skills, for example, हाँ भैया, ये आम कितने के हैं?; आप के भोजनालय में सबसे स्वादिष्ट व्यंजन कौन सा है?; मुझे दो रोटी के साथ एक दाल मक्खनी दे दीजिए; मुझे यह ज़्यादा पसंद हैं; यह बहुत महंगा है, दाम कुछ कम करोI

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing aspects of Hindi language and associated cultures to younger students or non-Hindi speakers through a range of activities, including games such as लोग, शहर और जानवर or folk dances such as भांगड़ा or डांडिया

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: working collaboratively to create a set of instructions or a procedure to demonstrate and explain activities or processes, such as recipes, dance steps, a simple science experiment, or nurturing a seed, for example, रोटी बनाना; बीज-पौधे लगाना-बीज अंकुरण की विधि: १. पहले बीज को गीली रुई में रखे, २. रोज़ रुई को गिला रखे और धुप लगाए; कागज़ का हवाई जहाज़ उड़ाना

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: stating preferences in a range of activities and interactions and reacting to others’ choices or indicating preferences between 2 or more objects, for example, क्या सच में? ज्यादातर लोगों को पसंद नहीं …; सेब, संतरा या अंगूर में से आपको कौन सा सबसे अच्छा लगता है? मुझे अंगूर पसंद है।

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking on different roles and responsibilities in the classroom or school environment, such as recycling monitor, calling the roll, distributing work, giving instructions, checking homework or the wearing of hats outside, for example, इस कूड़ेदान में बोतलें डालें; धूप है, तुम्हारी टोपी कहाँ है?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning presentations or performances for school assemblies or community events (e.g. होली; स्वतंत्रता दिवस; दिवाली; सदभावना दिवस), using expressions such as आज हम आप के सामने प्रस्तुत करने जा रहे हैं …

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: working together to solve puzzles and riddles; or to follow directions to real or imagined locations, using digital tools to access mapping applications, for example, आगे से दायें, फिर सीधे जाईए फिर दो गली छोडकर मुड़िये

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C02-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the process of working together to plan and execute an event or performance, and what they would do differently next time, for example, अगली बार मैं नाचने के बजाय गाना चाहूँगा …; मुझे तुम्हारा सुझाव बहुत पसंद आया …

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6C03 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting facts, figures and vocabulary from printed and digital texts, and using them to prepare a class discussion about topics such as healthy lifestyle or caring for the environment

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information from peers, community members or relatives to create an overview of selected trends, preferred modes of communication or social behaviours, and comparing responses with their own thoughts on similar issues, for example, जब आप छोटे थे तब लोग कैसे कपड़े पहनते थे?; आपके और हमारे स्कूल में क्या अंतर है?; कम्प्यूटर के बिना आप अपने दोस्तों से कैसे बात करते थे, फ़ोन / ईमेल / आमने सामने बातचीत / टेक्स्टिंग?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing a report or announcement, such as a weekend weather forecast or program of events for a festival or sports match, and writing a message to a family member or friend to ask them to participate, for example, रविवार को धूप है, क्या आप समुद्रतट पर चलेंगे?; शाम के ५ बजे स्वतंत्रता दिवस का कार्यक्रम होगा

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing an image of students eating lunch at a school in India or another Hindi-speaking region, and completing a ‘word-phrase-sentence’ thinking routine using information from the image before discussing their notes with a partner

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ stories and responding to them using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in Hindi

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing and comparing information accessed via videos, books and websites that reflect lifestyles in Hindi-speaking communities in different regions, for example, Fiji, Mauritius or Trinidad and Tobago, and presenting information in new ways, such as a digital display or a spoken, print or visual presentation to suit a specific audience

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing, describing and illustrating favourite comic book characters, superheroes and events, and identifying language or behaviours they associate with them, for example, चाचा चौधरी और साबू; विक्रम और वेताल; पिंकी और बबलू; अकबर-बीरबल के क़िस्से; चाचा चौधरी का दिमाग़ कम्प्यूटर से भी तेज़ चलता है; वेताल कहता है “तू बोला विक्रम, और मैं गया, हा हा हा।”

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing messages, morals and character traits featured in fables, songs and stories (e.g. परिश्रम का फल मीठा होता है; सूझबूझ से कठिन से कठिन कार्य भी संभव है), and incorporating them into their own imaginative texts

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating information about the school and surrounding area, and incorporating the facts in a persuasive advertisement to attract visitors or new students, for example, यह भोजनालय की व्यंजन-सूची है, आप इसमें से अपनी पसंद की सब्जी चुन लें

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E10 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to survey and compile information about others’ interests and preferences (e.g. favourite things, leisure activities, pets, language(s) spoken), and presenting findings in a range of formats such as mind maps, graphs, diagrams or an oral presentation

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C03-E11 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading or listening to a short text about a holiday destination or a location for an event or camp, and deciding as a class or in groups a list of what to bring or pack, categorising items in order of priority and justifying their reasons, for example, वहाँ ठंड होगी, इसलिए अपने साथ एक जैकेट भी रख लेना

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6C04 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Hindi in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: knowing that meaning is shaped not only by words but also by expression, gestures and the use of voice and tone, and that these variations occur in both formal and informal language

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use bilingual print dictionaries and translation apps to work out the meaning of unfamiliar words or sentences, and determining the reliability of these aids to accurately translate information

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining Hindi words, proverbs, idioms or expressions that they find challenging or humorous to non-Hindi-speakers, for example, पेट में चूहे दौड़ रहे हैं; दूर के ढोल सुहावने होते हैं

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between spoken and written forms of Hindi, identifying examples of colloquialisms, words and expressions used mainly in spoken language, for example, the non-standard मेरे को in place of the formal मुझे, or the use of मतलब … at the beginning of spoken utterances

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating texts such as signs, menu items or public announcements from Hindi to English, and vice versa, identifying words that convey the closest equivalent meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a class dictionary, word wall or word bank of Hindi words, expressions or loan words collected while travelling on an imaginary trip around Australia or overseas, noticing trends and the emergence of new words or ‘Hinglish’ terms

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C04-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying Hindi words or expressions that have embedded cultural meanings and considering Australian English words and expressions that may be misunderstood by Hindi speakers, such as ‘bring a plate’, ‘no worries’, ‘mate’, ‘dog’s breakfast’, and placing findings in a Venn diagram or chart

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6C05 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning ways to type words and sentences in Hindi using a keyboard and incorporating typed Devanāgarī script into a variety of texts

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating individual language-and-culture profiles, explaining which language(s) or dialects are spoken at home, with extended family, or in their social and community lives

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a multimodal profile of a local community, including facilities and events, for recent Hindi-speaking migrants to Australia, and using useful information and facts from websites or brochures, for example, भारतीय सुपरमार्केट रात नौ बजे तक खुला रहता है

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a class print or digital poster in Hindi, locating and describing a specific Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place in a local or regional context, or elsewhere in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating bilingual texts for non-Hindi speakers wanting to visit India or a Hindi-speaking region to assist with travel and communication, such as wordlists, common phrases, maps, menus and allergy cards, for example, मुझे मूँगफली से एलर्जी है

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing expressive texts such as narratives, poetry or personal commentaries, using mime, music and evocative language to convey concepts that are relevant to their own social worlds and interests, for example, मित्रता; प्रेम; दया; अतिथि-सत्कार; अनेकता में एकता

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting a familiar story, cartoon or poem to suit a younger or different kind of audience by including a new character, event or change of mood, for example, an Australian version of चाचा चौधरी; a lullaby that is exciting rather than soothing; or an alternative ending for a story

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating informative and imaginative texts for specific purposes and audiences, for example, a presentation for parents or guests about the benefits of learning a second or additional language, or to showcase their bilingual or multilingual experience

elaborations.name: VC2LH6C05-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with language features and simple devices appropriate to text type, such as descriptions in recounts or narratives, humour in comic verse, and persuasive language in advertisements

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6U01 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency and rhythm in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and pronouncing all the sounds in the Hindi Varnmala chart, including aspirated and unaspirated sounds, for example, च – छ; ट – ठ

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing the difference between unaspirated and aspirated sounds and practising aloud, such as क (e.g. करना) vs. ख (e.g. खाना)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to check the correct pronunciation of Hindi, and using voice-recording software to check their own tone and intonation to develop fluency

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that mispronouncing vowel sounds in Hindi can affect meaning, for example, ओर vs. और; में vs. मैं

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Hindi pronunciation of some words varies depending on the region, but the written form remains the same, for example, ‘much’ or ‘many’ is commonly pronounced as बहोत, but the standard spelling is बहुत

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing between the intonation patterns of requests and exclamations, for example, क्या मैं पानी पीने जा सकता हूँ? / कृपया मुझे पानी पीने जाने दीजिए।; वह पास हो गया!; क्या आप वहाँ जाएँगे?; तुम अच्छे बच्चे हो

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using active listening skills to determine intonation for statements and questions when no interrogative is used, for example, भूख लगी है। / भूख लगी है?; बाहर जा रहे हैं। / बाहर जा रहे हैं?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how new loan words are formed in Hindi, for example, the way in which English ‘t’ and ‘d’ sounds are represented normally as ट and ड, English ‘th’ sounds are replaced by थ, and English vowels such as short ‘a’ sounds are replaced by Hindi vowel sounds (e.g. डॉलर, not डालर)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U01-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the Hindi pronunciation and Devanāgarī spelling of loan words from English into Hindi, for example, अस्पताल/हस्पताल; अफ़सर; पलस्तर

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6U02 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use the Devanāgarī script and a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and practising the spelling of words in the Devanāgarī script that involve combinations of pronouns and postpositions that lose the inherent ‘a’ inside a word (e.g. उसका, सुनना, सुनता)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of past, present and future verb tenses (e.g. जाता था, जाता हूँ, जाऊँगा)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using adverbs in sentences to provide additional information (e.g. धीरे-धीरे, जल्दी में, दौड़ते हुए)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using singular and plural forms of nouns and pronouns (e.g. मैं/हम; यह/ये)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: conjugating a range of verbs according to gender, tense and tone, for example, विकास बाज़ार जाता है; दादाजी बाज़ार जाते हैं; विकास बाज़ार जाएगा; दादीजी बाज़ार जाएँगी

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and understanding how Hindi verbs indicate the idea of actions happening or being made to happen (e.g. बनना, बनाना, बनवाना)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple comparative and superlative forms of adjectives, for example, अधिक अच्छा / सबसे अच्छा / उससे अच्छा; उच्च / उच्चत्तर / उच्चत्तम

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E08 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of prepositions of location and place to give directions, for example, स्कूल बाग़ के पास है; मेरा घर दुकानों के पीछे है

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E09 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of interrogatives and questioning techniques to make formal and informal requests and obtain specific information, for example, आपकी किताबें कहाँ हैं?; यह डिब्बा कैसे खुलेगा?; वहाँ कौन खड़ा है?

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E10 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using negative forms of verbs and adjectives, for example, सोहन ने फिल्म नहीं देखी; झूठ कभी मत बोलो

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E11 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of conjunctions to connect different elements of a sentence and expand ideas, for example, राम ने खाना खाया और सो गया

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E12 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating events in time by using days of the week, months and ordinal numbers (e.g. पहला, दूसरा)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E13 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing typed and handwritten Hindi texts, noticing variations and reasons why texts and fonts can look different, for example, shape, spacing and proportion

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U02-E14 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the rules for half consonants (क्, च्, ज्) to form words (e.g. बच्चा, कच्चा, अच्छा, मक्खी, राज्य, कद्दु) and sentences (e.g. आज दिन बहुत अच्छा है)

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LH6U03 - Hindi F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare Hindi language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E01 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the significance and cultural importance of features of different types of texts in Hindi and English, for example, salutations, greetings and conveying respect, such as ‘Dear/to …’, आदरणीय, पूज्य, मान्यवर, महोदय, प्रिय मित्र

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E02 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a graphic organiser, poster, mind map or Venn diagram to illustrate differences in Hindi and English grammar and textual conventions, for example, the absence of articles and contractions, the use of different word order and the use of some adjectives as verbs in Hindi, and the absence of grammatical gender and the use of contractions in English

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E03 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing features of familiar genres of Hindi and English texts, and noticing similarities and differences between language features such as the use of tense, word order, sentence structure and common phrases in particular text types, for example, ‘Once upon a time …’ – एक समय की बात है …; ‘many years ago’ – बहुत साल पहले

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E04 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how the choice of language features and text organisation reflect the purpose and audience of different types of text in Hindi and English, for example, when giving an oral presentation to the class, talking to friends in the schoolyard, going shopping or visiting the doctor

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E05 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the influence of Sanskrit on Hindi by noticing how Sanskrit words have been adopted and adapted in different ways (e.g. कर्म, रात्रि, सर्प, काम, रात, साँप), and exploring the influence of other languages (e.g. ड्रामा, सरकस, गलीचा, किताब)

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E06 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some English loan words originate from Hindi (e.g. jungle, bandana, dinghy), and that Hindi has loan words from English (e.g. गोल, कैच, पॉप रैप, पास्ता, नूडल्स, केचप/सॉस, माउस, कीबोर्ड, स्क्रीन), and discussing reasons why languages borrow from each other

elaborations.name: VC2LH6U03-E07 - Hindi F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use simple metalanguage, in both Hindi and English, to understand and discuss grammatical structures and features of texts, for example, संज्ञा – noun; सर्वनाम – pronoun; क्रिया – verb; विशेषण – adjective
